record.paper_title: Open Problems in Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient Algorithms for Unconstrained Optimization
record.original_question: In nonlinear conjugate gradient methods for minimizing a continuously differentiable objective f, formulas for the conjugate gradient parameter beta_k are usually built from gradient norms, differences y_k = g_{k+1} - g_k, displacements s_k = x_{k+1} - x_k, and related inner products. How can one use objective-function values such as f(x_k) and f(x_{k+1}) directly in the definition of beta_k to construct new conjugate gradient algorithms with good convergence and practical performance?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. How can we use the function values in βk to generate new conjugate gradient algorithms? ... As we can see in the formula for βk the difference f(xk)−f(xk+1) is not used at all.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the unconstrained minimization problem
    min { f(x) : x ∈ R^n },
where f : R^n → R is continuously differentiable with gradient g(x) = ∇f(x). A nonlinear conjugate gradient method generates iterates
    x_{k+1} = x_k + α_k d_k,
with d_0 = -g_0 and, for k ≥ 1,
    d_{k+1} = -g_{k+1} + β_k d_k,
where α_k > 0 is a step length (typically chosen via a line search satisfying the standard Wolfe or strong Wolfe conditions) and β_k ∈ R is the conjugate gradient parameter. Classical choices of β_k (Hestenes–Stiefel, Fletcher–Reeves, Polak–Ribière–Polyak, Dai–Yuan, Liu–Storey, conjugate descent, etc.) are functions only of the gradients g_k = g(x_k) and g_{k+1}, the difference y_k = g_{k+1} - g_k, the displacement s_k = x_{k+1} - x_k, and inner products and norms built from these vectors; they do not involve the objective function values f(x_k) and f(x_{k+1}).

Problem. Design a nonlinear conjugate gradient algorithm in which the parameter β_k explicitly depends on the function-value information f(x_k) and f(x_{k+1}) (for instance through the difference f(x_k) - f(x_{k+1}) or quantities derived from it), prove that the resulting method generates descent directions and is globally convergent on a suitable class of objective functions under a standard line-search condition, and demonstrate that it offers competitive numerical performance compared with established conjugate gradient schemes.
artifact.status_search_result: Several conjugate gradient algorithms incorporate function-value information indirectly via modified secant conditions, e.g. using z_k = y_k + (η_k/||s_k||^2) s_k with η_k = 2(f_k - f_{k+1}) + (g_k + g_{k+1})^T s_k (as in accelerated hybrid CG schemes). These constitute partial progress, but a fully developed family of CG methods in which β_k depends directly and intrinsically on f(x_k), f(x_{k+1}) — with global convergence theory and demonstrated competitive performance — remains an active research direction rather than a definitively closed problem.

status_evidence.title: Accelerated hybrid conjugate gradient algorithm with modified secant condition
status_evidence.snippet: η_k = 2(f_k - f_{k+1}) + (g_k + g_{k+1})^T s_k is used inside a modified secant condition driving the β_k computation.
status_evidence.claim: Function values appear indirectly in β_k through a modified secant condition, indicating partial progress on the problem.

status_evidence.title: Hybrid Conjugate Gradient Algorithm for Unconstrained Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: β_k^C = (1-θ_k)β_k^{HS} + θ_k β_k^{DY} is a convex combination of standard parameters that do not directly use f-values.
status_evidence.claim: Standard β_k formulas remain based on gradient and displacement information, not directly on function values.
